references.text: Parallel text about the Day of Atonement that also describes the day as a 'Sabbath of solemn rest' (שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן) where the people must fast ('afflict their souls') as an eternal statute.
Uses the same expression 'Sabbath of solemn rest' (שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן) in connection with the sabbatical year for the land.
Uses the expression 'Sabbath of solemn rest' (שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן) regarding the weekly Sabbath, showing the connection between the Sabbath and holy rest.
Another reference to 'Sabbath of solemn rest' (שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן) that emphasizes holy rest as an eternal ordinance.
Describes the Day of Atonement and the command to afflict one's soul (וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם), parallel with Leviticus 16:31.
The prophet Isaiah discusses the meaning of fasting and uses the expression 'afflict one's soul' (עַנּוֹת נֶפֶשׁ), which connects to the fast of the Day of Atonement.
David mentions that he afflicted his soul with fasting (עִנֵּיתִי בַצּוֹם נַפְשִׁי), the same concept as in the command for the Day of Atonement.
The book of Hebrews explains how Christ fulfilled the rituals of the Day of Atonement by entering the Most Holy Place once for all with his own blood.
Reference to 'the fast' (τὴν νηστείαν), which is the Day of Atonement, showing that this day was still observed in New Testament times.
